Before we start

Install once, then one shared dataset

install.packages(c(
  "tidyverse", "table1", "gtsummary", "labelled", "gt", "flextable",
  "janitor", "skimr", "tidylog", "here", "beepr", "reprex",
  "highcharter", "patchwork", "gganimate", "gifski",
  "wesanderson", "ghibli", "MetBrewer", "taylor",
  "ggsci", "paletteer", "colorspace",
  "NHANES", "palmerpenguins", "gapminder"
))

Data: NHANES (US survey, 2009–2012), palmerpenguins, gapminder, plus datasets that ship with highcharter and base R.

  • nh is used all morning: adults with a diabetes answer.
  • Why distinct(ID)? The NHANES package repeats some participants. janitor will show us.
1

Tables

From a raw data frame to a publication-ready Table 1 and Table 2, without retyping a single number.

table1
gtsummary

Tables

Two packages, two jobs

table1gtsummary
SyntaxA formula: table1(~ x + y | group, data)A pipe: data |> tbl_summary(by = group)
p-valuesNot built inadd_p() picks the test and footnotes it
RegressionNotbl_regression(), tbl_uvregression(), tbl_merge()
StylesA few built-in CSS themesJournal themes for JAMA, Lancet and NEJM
ExportCopy from the Viewer, or t1flex() to WordWord, PowerPoint, PDF, HTML, image
Best forA fast descriptive look at your dataTables that go in a paper or thesis

Both read the same variable labels, so the prep step on the next slide works for both.

labelled

Tables · prep

Label once, every table uses it

look_for() doubles as a data dictionary. Notice SmokeNow: 2,598 missing, because NHANES only asked people who had smoked 100+ cigarettes.

table1

Tables · table1

A Table 1 in one line

Formula: rows ~ Age + Gender + …, split into columns | Diabetes. The labels from the last slide become the row names; missing values get their own row.

table1

Tables · table1

Nested columns and your choice of statistics

Need p-values or a regression table? That's where gtsummary comes in.

gtsummary

Tables · gtsummary · 1

Build a Table 1 one line at a time

gtsummary

Tables · gtsummary · 2

Choose the statistics

all_continuous() and all_categorical() select variables by type, like tidyselect helpers. A dichotomous variable gets one row instead of two.

gtsummary

Tables · gtsummary · 3

Regression models, formatted

exponentiate = TRUE turns log-odds into odds ratios. Reference levels get a dash, and the variable labels carry over from the data.

gtsummary

Tables · gtsummary · 4

Unadjusted vs adjusted, side by side

tbl_uvregression() fits one model per variable. Sex goes from OR 1.14 (p = 0.2) unadjusted to 1.43 (p < 0.001) once age, BMI and activity are in the model.

gtsummary

Tables · gtsummary · 5

Match the journal's style

A theme applies to tables built after you set it. reset_gtsummary_theme() goes back to the default.

gtsummary

Tables · gtsummary · 6

More table types

Also worth knowing: tbl_svysummary() takes survey weights. NHANES is a complex survey, so real prevalence estimates need it.

gtsummary

Tables · gtsummary · 7

Get tables out of R

To Word

final |>
  as_gt() |>
  gt::gtsave("table1_nhanes.docx")

Opens as a real, editable Word table. .html, .pdf and .png work too.

table1 to Word

table1(~ Age + BMI | Diabetes, data = tab) |>
  t1flex() |>
  flextable::save_as_docx(path = "table1_quick.docx")

table1 goes through flextable.

Numbers inside a sentence

Console

          
In Quarto or R Markdown, write `r inline_text(final, ...)` in your text and the number updates whenever the data do.

Fewer headaches
Pipes that narrate, paths that just work

  

    

    

      
here(): no more setwd()

      
library(here)

dat <- read_csv(here("data", "nhanes.csv"))
ggsave(here("figures", "bmi.png"))

      
Builds paths from your RStudio Project folder, so the same script runs on a Mac, a PC, or your TA's laptop.

      
tidylog: load it after dplyr. The join tab shows 4,653 rows turning into 7,233 because of repeat IDs.

    

  






  
Lightning round
Small joys

  

    
beepr
Hear when code finishes

      
fit <- glm(Diabetes ~ Age + BMI, data = nh,
           family = binomial)
beepr::beep("fanfare")

    
reprex
Ask for help well

      
Copy your broken code, run reprex::reprex(), and paste. Code and output arrive together, formatted for Canvas, Slack or Stack Overflow.

    
datapasta
Paste a table as code

      
Copy cells from Excel or a web page. RStudio Addins → "Paste as tribble" writes the tribble() for you.

    
styler
Tidy your code style

      
Addins → "Style active file" fixes spacing and indentation to tidyverse style in one click.

highcharter

    
highcharter · 9
Finishing touches

  

    
Let readers download it

      
p |> hc_exporting(enabled = TRUE)

      
Adds a menu for PNG, SVG, PDF and the underlying CSV.

    
Titles, captions, credits

      
p |>
  hc_subtitle(text = "Gapminder, 2007") |>
  hc_caption(text = "Bubble size = population") |>
  hc_credits(enabled = TRUE, text = "BIOS 544")

    
Share it as a web page

      
htmlwidgets::saveWidget(p, "wealth_health.html")

      
One file anyone can open. It also drops straight into an HTML Quarto or R Markdown report.

    
Find more ideas

      
The highcharter showcase has the full code for the measles heatmap, weather radial and Pokémon treemap, plus a lot more.

      
Interactive charts belong in HTML reports, not PDF manuscripts.

  






  
patchwork
gganimate

    
Also worth knowing
Two ggplot add-ons

  

    

      
patchwork: arrange plots with | and /

      
library(patchwork)

p1 <- ggplot(nh, aes(BMI)) + geom_histogram()
p2 <- ggplot(nh, aes(Diabetes, BMI)) + geom_boxplot()
p3 <- ggplot(nh, aes(Age, BMI)) + geom_point(alpha = .2)

(p1 | p2) / p3 +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")

      
Panel labels A, B, C for free: a manuscript figure in one line.

    

    

      
gganimate: the Hans Rosling chart

      
library(gganimate)

ggplot(gapminder, aes(gdpPercap, lifeExp,
                      size = pop, color = continent)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(title = "Year: {frame_time}") +
  transition_time(year)

      
Save with anim_save("rosling.gif"). Rendering takes about 30 seconds.

Emory

    
Make your own
An Emory palette for your slides

  

    

      

      
Console

      

      
p + scale_fill_manual(
  values = colorRampPalette(emory)(5))

      
colorRampPalette() is base R. Use it for a lab palette, a journal's colors or a poster.

Four things with NHANES

  

    
1
Table 1, twice

      
Summarize Age, BMI, SleepHrsNight and Education by PhysActive, first with table1, then with tbl_summary() |> add_p(). Give BMI a label.

    
2
Table 2

      
Fit glm(PhysActive ~ Age + Gender + BMI). Merge tbl_uvregression() with tbl_regression() and save it to Word.

highcharter

      
Make a heatmap of mean BMI by AgeDecade and Education. Add a theme.
